parallel.requirements: Recognized the benchmark as a black-box reimplementation of tui-journal 0.16.1 with no source lookup, no wrapper, and no binary analysis.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned final implementation but delegated exhaustive behavioral probing to a workflow split across ten broad areas plus a planned gap critic.
parallel.implementation: Built a Rust Cargo skeleton and implemented partial TUI infrastructure including style, buffer, unicode width, layout, terminal pieces, and main.rs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact included the partial source tree, build outputs, explore helper scripts, docs, assets, and original executable, but artifact validation reported ok false.
parallel.verification: Performed spot CLI, TUI, geometry, terminal, and build probes while child probes ran, but no complete evaluator-aligned integrated verification closed before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with returncode 143; the workflow was killed with result null and official evaluation reported compile_failed with all 1839 tests not run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same black-box reimplementation task and used only bundled documentation plus normal executable interaction.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept probing, implementation, test fixture creation, and packaging in one agent with workflows and delegation disabled.
serial.implementation: Produced a broader Rust source tree covering config, sys, json, TUI, CLI, paths, theme, toml, main, compile.sh, notes, and golden-screen tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Packaged a source tree that artifact validation accepted as ok true, including compile.sh and broad module coverage.
serial.verification: Created golden fixtures and scenario scripts for TUI states and compared behavior locally, but official evaluation still failed before running tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial process also timed out with returncode 143 and official evaluation reported compile_failed with all 1839 tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the same black-box reverse-engineering obligation, including the ban on source lookup, wrappers, and binary analysis.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the identical prompt and recognized the same requirement to reimplement from observed binary behavior and bundled docs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; the difference is how the parallel run allocated exploration and budget after recognizing the requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent created a harness and launched a workflow whose AREAS array divided behavior into ten broad probe domains handled by child agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had workflows disabled and no delegation, so one agent retained local ownership of probing, implementation, tests, and packaging.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delegated breadth-first exploration while the parent implemented; serial kept all findings and coding in one thread and avoided child lifecycle overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs asked each probe to write Markdown notes under /workspace/explore/notes and return structured summaries, with unique session/home instructions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent accumulated its observations directly into local notes and implementation files, without cross-agent handoff contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel interface was an exploration-note handoff that never produced a final aggregate, whereas serial's observations remained immediately available to the same implementer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a Cargo project, build.rs, main.rs, and several low-level TUI modules, but the artifact list shows a narrow partial source tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a broader application skeleton with config, sys, json, TUI, cli, paths, theme, toml, main, compile.sh, and golden test assets.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial reached more of the required app surface in source files and packaging, while parallel spent more closure window on workflow-backed exploration and remained less assembled.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow state ended with result null, status killed, repeated stall retries, one child in error, and many children still in progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle to join; protocol validation reports zero workflow calls and zero child logs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a costly unresolved child-result lifecycle; serial had no external result retrieval point and therefore no trapped workflow aggregate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel's final artifact included implementation files plus an explore directory with probe helpers and notes, and artifact validation was false.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's artifact validation was true and its members include tests, notes, source modules, compile.sh, docs, assets, and executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delivery was less clean and less package-valid; serial's final tree was broader and accepted by artifact validation even though official compilation still failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified some build and behavior fragments but reached official evaluation as compile_failed with all 1839 tests not run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created golden-screen tests and scenario fixtures, but the official evaluation also ended compile_failed with all 1839 tests not run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial invested more in local acceptance fixtures; neither run reached evaluator-executed tests because both submissions failed compilation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 35 subagents, 1 workflow, 1,404,815 workflow child tokens, and 550 child-tool calls, then timed out with returncode 143.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents or workflow tasks, ran direct tool calls, and also timed out with returncode 143 after a package-valid artifact was captured.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel budget was consumed by a large stalled fan-out in addition to parent work; serial spent its budget directly on implementation and packaged more of the app before the same official failure class.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed cell/status.json evaluations are not discordant: parallel and serial both have solution_passed false, error_code compile_failed, and 1839 tests not run. The task-solving difference is process and artifact quality, not official pass/fail: parallel spent a large fraction of the budget on a broad stalled workflow and delivered a partial, artifact-invalid tree; serial kept the work local, implemented more modules and tests, and produced an artifact-valid package, but still did not compile under the official evaluator.
parallel_contributors: Broad ten-area workflow fan-out with repeated stalled retries consumed child-token and tool-call budget before a usable aggregate returned.
The parent continued implementing but closed with a narrower partial source tree and artifact_validation.ok false.
serial_contributors: Serial workflows were disabled, so task knowledge and implementation remained in one control flow.
Serial produced a broader package-valid source tree and local golden fixtures before timing out.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both final submissions had ordinary unresolved build or implementation defects, as shown by the shared compile_failed official outcome.
The exact compiler defect is not expanded in the available status summary; the evaluator did not run the 1839 tests in either mode.
evaluator_effects: The current completed status.json evaluation supersedes aggregate interpretations and establishes both_fail rather than a discordant result.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized parallel-side adverse process difference, not an explanation for a pass/fail split

The parent launched one workflow that fanned out ten broad behavioral probes across CLI, config, themes, both backends, and multiple TUI surfaces, while the parent continued implementation. The workflow state then records repeated stall retries, 1,404,815 child tokens, 550 child tool calls, result null, and status killed. That collective breadth and retry behavior consumed the finite run budget before the parent could assemble a package-valid, complete implementation. The serial control used no workflows and produced a broader package-valid source tree, although it still failed official compilation.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel run spent a large child-agent budget on stalled probes and ended with a killed workflow, returncode 143, artifact_validation.ok false, and a partial final source tree instead of the package-valid broader implementation that the serial run reached.
candidates.near_match_reason: Several child logs show interruptions and the workflow ended killed, but those are downstream of the same broad fan-out and stall-retry budget episode. The directly actionable boundary is reducing or sequencing the excessive probe fan-out, not separately classifying each stopped child.
